Attestation.description:
How much trust a measurement record has earned.

A self-reported record starts life unattested; CI moves it. Only `confirmed` and `confirmed-static` are passes. The `unwitnessed-*` values are explicitly **not** tamper accusations — conflating them with `divergent` is the false-divergence epidemic of PREMORTEM T1/Story 1.

oneOf.description: CI recomputed the deterministic compare set and every per-result digest matched.
Fork tier (PREMORTEM T5): CI recomputed from an unprivileged job with no self-report available to compare against. A pass, labelled as the weaker one it is.
Digests disagree on an equal `(base_oid, head_oid)` tuple at an equal measurement regime — or a tamper signal fired. The first-class tamper outcome.
No CI recompute happened. Neutral, not negative.
The regimes differ (engine, grammar, or git version skew), so the digests were never comparable. Never `divergent` — PREMORTEM S4.

The claimed base is an ancestor of the trusted branch — a stale base or a rebase, not an attack. A non-tamper outcome that is still **not a pass**: the record stays self-reported and never counts downstream (PLAN R2-4).

The head was an uncommitted tree, so no verifier can ever witness it.

# Why this is not the generic `unwitnessed`

`unwitnessed` is documented above as *"No CI recompute happened. Neutral, not negative"* — a statement about the past, and one that stops being true the moment CI runs. This one is a statement about what is possible: CI cannot check out somebody's working tree, so a record measured against one is **permanently** unwitnessable, and no future run changes that.

Collapsing the two would tell an operator to wait for an attestation that is never coming, which is the actor-observability defect the `unwitnessed-*` family already exists to avoid: `unwitnessed-version-skew` and `unwitnessed-base-mismatch` are both specific causes kept out of the generic bucket for exactly this reason.

Like the rest of the family it is **not an accusation** and **not a pass**. A measurement of uncommitted work is real, useful to its author, and outside the trust boundary by construction (P5b mini-G2 ruling).

AttestationBlock.description: The trust half of a record.

compare.description: Present once a compare has been attempted.

value.description: How much trust this record has earned.

CacheState.description: Whether the cache served this result.

oneOf.description: Served from a populated cache.
Computed with an empty cache.
The cache was populated but this key was absent.

CompareContext.description:
The git tuple every measurement is pinned to.

`base_oid` and `head_oid` are required, never optional: a record that cannot say what it measured cannot be compared, and an uncomparable record that looks comparable is how a fabricated base gets laundered (PLAN B3, R2-4).

The **base is always a commit**. A dirty base is refused everywhere — by `git::resolve`, by `ChangedSet::enumerate`, and here by contract — because "compared against uncommitted content" is a comparison nothing can stand in for. Only the head has a kind.

base_oid.description: Full 40-character base commit OID. Always a commit.

base_resolution.description: How the base was arrived at, e.g. `merge-base`, `explicit`, `worktree`.

git_version.description: `git --version` output of the git that resolved this tuple.

head_oid.description:
The head's identity, of the kind [`Self::head_kind`] names: a full 40-character commit OID for `commit` — the PR head SHA, never the synthetic merge ref (PLAN B3) — or the content hash of an uncommitted snapshot otherwise.

**Read `head_kind` before interpreting this.** It was unconditionally a commit OID at `schema_version` 1, which is why 2 exists.

CompareOutcome.description: The result of comparing a self-report against a recompute.

flag_disagreements.description:
Metric ids the two sides paired but disagreed about the `deterministic` flag on.

The verifier's flag decides compare-set membership, so a disagreement changes nothing about the outcome — but it is exactly the shape an attempt to duck the compare would leave, and a signal nobody can see is a signal that does not exist. Entries here are worth a look; they are not an accusation, since an engine version can legitimately change whether a metric is seed-free.

matched.description: Metric ids whose digests were compared and agreed.

mismatched.description: Metric ids whose digests were compared and disagreed.

regime_equal.description: Did the measurement regimes match? Checked second; unequal means `unwitnessed-version-skew`, never `divergent` (PREMORTEM S4).

tuple_equal.description: Did the `(base_oid, head_oid)` tuples match? Checked first, so that a mismatch is classified rather than reported as divergence (PLAN R2-4).

unpaired.description: Metric ids present on one side only.

Completeness.description: How complete a measurement is. Absence of data is always said out loud rather than reported as a zero.

oneOf.description: Everything the engine set out to measure was measured.
The fast lane hit its cold cap and spilled to async, or an engine was skipped. Some results are missing and named as missing.
The parser produced ERROR/MISSING nodes over part of the input. Results so marked never drive MED+ and never carry full-confidence claims (PREMORTEM T3).
The inputs needed did not exist — a shallow clone with no history for a process metric, for instance. Never a fabricated zero (PLAN P4).

EngineClass.description:
Whether running an engine executes repository code.

Enforced at the trait boundary, not by convention: the sandbox of P7 keys off this, and a `code-exec` engine may never run in a context that promised only static analysis (Codex #19).

oneOf.description: Reads bytes and parses. Never spawns repository code.
Runs code from the repository under test. Requires the sandbox.

EngineFamily.description: The five engine families. Fixed in v1: every `MeasurementRegime` variant and every registry file maps onto exactly one.

oneOf.description: tree-sitter size and complexity metrics (P2).
Token-level duplication detection (P3).
Static gaming detectors (P3).
git-history signals: churn, age, ownership, coupling (P4).
Coverage-report parsing, negative signal only (P4).

EvidenceRef.description: The evidence a number stands on, resolved from the registry at report time.

citation.description: Short citation key; the registry holds the full citation.

does_not_predict.description: The honesty field. What this number is *not* evidence for.

stale.description: True once the claim is past its expiry. Set by the registry loader against the run date, surfaced in every rendering, and never silent (PREMORTEM S2). Excluded from digests precisely because it is time-dependent.

EvidenceTier.description: Evidence strength for a claim, as graded in `docs/metric-families.csv`.

oneOf.description: Validated against outcomes at scale.
Published validation, narrower population or weaker linkage.
Weak or contested on its own.
Critiqued; not to be used as a headline.
Novel and unvalidated. Motivated by evidence, not yet supported by it.

Freshness.description: Timing and cache metadata. Excluded from every digest.

HeadKind.description:
What kind of thing the head of a measured range is.

# Why this exists rather than a commit OID standing in for a working tree

The state the product exists for is an agent that has just written a change and not committed it. Measuring it needs a head, and the working tree has no commit OID — so there were only ever two honest options, and the tempting third one is a vulnerability.

The tempting one: write `HEAD`'s OID into `head_oid` and carry on. That produces a record which passes the verifier's tuple-equality check while describing bytes that were never committed, so the verifier recomputes the *commit*, gets different numbers, and reports `divergent` on honest work. That is the R2-4 laundering path from one side and PREMORTEM Story 1's false accusation from the other, and P1's `git::resolve` refused to build a `CompareContext` from a dirty endpoint precisely to keep it shut.

So the head says what it **is**. An uncommitted head carries the content hash of its own snapshot, which no commit OID can collide with in practice and which nothing downstream will mistake for one, because this field says not to. [`crate::compare::classify`] reads it before it reads anything else and refuses to compare, so a dirty record can never be accused.

oneOf.description: A commit. The only kind a verifier can check out and recompute.
An uncommitted working tree, including anything staged. `head_oid` is the content hash of the dirty snapshot, never a commit OID.
The index alone — staged content, with unstaged edits excluded. `head_oid` is the content hash of that snapshot.

Invocation.description: Ledger dimensions. Queryable by `andon ledger stats` (P8).

iteration.description: Which pass around the agent loop this is, for the iteration cap.

model.description: Model identifier, when the harness discloses one.

InvocationSource.description:
Who or what asked for this measurement.

A ledger dimension, and the evidence for PREMORTEM A2: a tool that is installed but never invoked shows up here as an empty `agent-initiated` column. P6's acceptance criterion counts these directly.

oneOf.description: A harness hook fired — the gate-shaped path.
An agent chose to call the MCP tool without a hook forcing it.
A human ran the CLI.
The CI verifier recomputing.

IterationState.description: Loop-iteration accounting, per branch, held in tool state so it survives session restarts (APPROACH graft 5).

cap.description: From the policy field, never a hardcode.

count.description: Passes taken on this branch so far.

escalated.description: True once the cap fired and the verdict became `escalate_to_human`.

oneOf.description: Sub-second static diff measurement.
Long-running work returning a job handle.

MeasurementRegime.description:
The configuration tuple for one engine family.

`BTreeMap` throughout, never `HashMap`: iteration order reaches the canonical serializer, and randomized ordering is one of the three independent byte-nondeterminism sources named in PREMORTEM Story 1.

oneOf.description: tree-sitter parsing engines (P2).

grammars.description: Language name to vendored grammar version, e.g. `typescript` -> `0.21.0`.

spec_revision.description: Revision of the clean-room metric specification implemented.

oneOf.description: Token clone detection (P3).
Static tamper detectors (P3).

detector_set_revision.description: Which detectors were active, as a revision of the set.

rule_pack_version.description: Version of the suppression/threshold rule pack.

oneOf.description: git-history signals (P4).

git_version.description: Captured from `git --version`; part of the regime because git's rename-detection defaults change across releases.

history_window_days.description: History window in days, from policy.

oneOf.description: Coverage-report parsers (P4). Parse-only, never executing.

parser_versions.description: Report format to parser version, e.g. `lcov` -> `1.0`.

MeasurementResult.description: One measured number, with everything needed to trust it.

claim_id.description: The evidence claim this number stands on. The registry lint fails the build if it does not resolve (PLAN P0/graft 3).

completeness.description: How complete this particular result is.

delta.description: Change against the base. `None` where a delta is meaningless.

deterministic.description:
Whether this result is seed-free and reproducible. Seeded or timing-dependent results are CI-authoritative only (APPROACH graft 2).

On a **self-report this is a claim, not a grant of exemption**. Compare-set membership is decided by the verifier's own copy of this flag: the field is outside [`ResultDigestInput`] and therefore unsigned, so honouring a self-report's `false` would let any result be excused from the compare by setting one boolean. A disagreement between the two sides is recorded in [`CompareOutcome::flag_disagreements`].

engine_class.description: Whether producing it executed repository code.

evidence.description: What this number does and does not support, resolved from the registry.

freshness.description: Timing and cache metadata. Never enters a digest.

measurement_regime.description: The engine-and-configuration tuple it was produced under.

metric_class.description: Whether the agent can act on it inside its own change.

severity.description: How serious, after policy. Excluded from the digest — the verifier computes its own from base-commit policy.

MetricClass.description:
Whether a finding is something the agent that made the change can act on.

The uninstall loop of PREMORTEM A4 comes from blocking on metrics nobody can fix in the diff. Policy may only escalate to MED+ on `diff-actionable` metrics, and `context-informational` findings are exempt from the iteration counter.

oneOf.description: Fixable inside the change being measured.
True and worth knowing, but about the surrounding code. Never blocks.

MetricValue.description:
A measured value.

Adjacently tagged so the type is explicit on the wire and a consumer never has to guess whether `3` was a count or a rounded ratio. Counts are integers and stay exact through canonical serialization (PLAN P5b: "counts always exact"); `Ratio` is the only float, and it is quantized on the way out and on the way back in.

oneOf.description: An exact non-negative count.
An exact signed quantity, e.g. a delta.
A proportion or rate, finite and quantized to [`RATIO_DECIMAL_PLACES`].
An elapsed time.
A boolean outcome, e.g. whether a detector fired.
A categorical or free-text value.

RecordKind.description: Whether a record is a self-report or a verifier's attestation.

oneOf.description: Written by the agent-side binary to `refs/notes/andon-measure`.
Written by the CI verifier to `refs/notes/andon-attest`.

Reserved.description:
Fields reserved so that monorepo and orchestrator support (VISION §3.3) land without a breaking schema change.

Always serialized, `null` when unset, so the shape of a record never varies with content.

blob_oid.description: The git blob OID the bytes came from. Present for every result in the compare set — the compared lane reads blobs, never the worktree, which is what makes a digest checkout-independent (PREMORTEM T1).

kind.description: Granularity: repository, change, file, or function.

line_span.description: Line range within the file, where the metric is line-scoped.

path.description: Repository-relative path with forward slashes, as git spells it. Never a filesystem path: worktree separators and case-folding differ per OS.

symbol.description: Function or class name, where the metric is scoped below file level.

ScopeKind.description: What granularity a result was measured at.

oneOf.description: The repository as a whole.
The change as a whole — the delta-first default.
One file.
One function or method.

Severity.description: Finding severity. "MED+" throughout the plan means `Medium` or above.

oneOf.description: Reported for context; never acted on.
Worth mentioning. Advises, never blocks.
The bottom of the MED+ band.
A strong finding on a diff-actionable metric.
Tamper signals and test failures under conservative defaults.

Substitution.description:
What was measured, when it was not what was asked for.

PREMORTEM A1 is a first command that returns nothing. The no-diff fallback answers it by measuring the last merged change — and the *saying so* is the load-bearing half, because a tool that quietly measures something other than what was asked for has told the reader a falsehood about what the numbers are about.

asked_for.description: What the caller's arguments resolved to, in the caller's own terms.

because.description: Why, in one sentence, for a reader who has only the report.

TamperSignal.description:
Deterministic signals that a number moved for a reason other than the code getting better.

Seven of these are the P3 detector suite (six from the metric catalogue plus the parse-error delta of PREMORTEM T3). `base-fabrication` is different in kind: it is raised by the git/attest lane, not by a content detector, when a record claims a base that is not an ancestor of the trusted branch (R2-4).

oneOf.description: `noqa` / `eslint-disable` / equivalent density rising in the diff.
Tests deleted or marked skipped.
Coverage-exclusion configuration widened.
New tests that execute code without asserting on it.
Thresholds edited in tool configuration inside the measured change.
A hard-coded lookup table standing in for an implementation.
Parse errors rose, hiding code from the static engines (PREMORTEM T3).
The claimed base is not an ancestor of the trusted branch, or is an unknown OID. Raised by the verifier; forces `divergent` (PLAN R2-4).

ToolIdentity.description: Which binary produced the record, and whether it was one we trust to measure itself (PREMORTEM S3).

attested_release.description: True when this binary is an attested release. False means the bootstrap exception is in force and the self-measurement is provisional.

build_oid.description: Commit the binary was built from.

Verdict.description:
What an actor is told to do about a change.

Deliberately categorical: PRE-DECISIONS non-goal 1 bars a composite score, forever. There is no numeric quality value anywhere in this schema for an agent to optimize against.

oneOf.description: Nothing above the policy's advisory floor.
Findings worth reporting that must not stop the line.
The line stops. Reserved for tamper signals, test failures, and MED+ findings on diff-actionable metrics.
The iteration cap fired, or a finding is real but not agent-fixable. A human decides; the agent must not keep grinding (PREMORTEM A4/S6).

VerdictReason.description: One reason a verdict is what it is.

iteration.description: Where this run sits against the iteration cap.

reasons.description: Why, one entry per contributing cause.

VerifierIdentity.description: Who attested. v1 trust is GitHub Actions provenance, not a signature — anyone with push access can write the attest ref (VISION §5, advisor F4).

run_ref.description: Workflow run URL or equivalent provenance pointer.

trusted_base_oid.description: The base the verifier resolved for itself, never the agent-claimed one.

description: One `andon measure` run, or one verifier recompute of the same change.

attestation.description: The trust half: attestation value, tamper signals, compare detail.

compare_context.description: The `(base_oid, head_oid)` tuple, required on every record (PLAN B3).

completeness.description: Record-level completeness, the weakest of the results'.

invocation.description: Ledger dimensions: who asked, through what, on which pass.

policy_hash.description: Digest of the policy in force. A record-level field and deliberately **not** part of any per-result digest — see [`ResultDigestInput`].

reserved.description: Fields reserved for monorepo and orchestrator support.

substitution.description:
Present exactly when something other than the caller's request was measured. Absent on every ordinary run.

A record-level field, and deliberately **not** part of any per-result digest — the same placement and the same reason as `policy_hash`. It describes how the measurement was arrived at, not what was measured, so putting it inside `ResultDigestInput` would make an announcement change every number's identity.

It is a field rather than a log line because the caveat has to survive the terminal. `cli::resolve`'s own documentation says the substitution "must appear in every rendering of the record — the reason it is a value rather than a log line", and it could not: `andon report` on a record produced by the fallback printed the numbers with no sign that they were about a different change from the one asked for. A caveat that lives only in the process that produced it does not exist for the reader who has only the record, which is most readers.

unreadable_paths.description:
Changed paths no engine could read, so nothing in `results` describes them. Empty on every ordinary run.

Durable for the reason the exit code is not enough on its own: `measure` exits 1 when this is non-empty, and then `report`, `--json`, the HTML report and the agent profile all read the saved record and exited 0 having lost the fact. A `pass` over bytes nobody read has the shape of a clean measurement and is not one — the project's rule about absences, applied to the record rather than only to the run.
